## Target and input record

If those records do not identify a target, return a candidate inventory for the target maintainer to select; do not treat the Skills checkout or a toy emitter as the intended deployment.

## Owners and handoffs

Surveyor maps each emitter to its event declaration and reachable call sites. Solidity Auditor reviews that map under #1361. Fizz builds and runs the differential harness. Hermes reviews the resulting executable reference against `CMP-10`; its acceptance must name the suite digest and limits. Elenchus receives each reproducible divergence. Alexandria preserves admitted capture inputs; it does not derive the emitter map.

## Required work

Generate a Foundry suite for a target whose events are emitted through hand-written assembly `log1`, `log2` and `log3` rather than the compiler's `emit`. For every emitter, fuzz its full argument domain and compare the recorded log against a reference emission of the same declared event through high-level `emit`: topic0, topic count, each indexed topic and the ABI-encoded data must be byte-identical. Any difference is a counterexample preserved as a specimen. Include ABI-type edge values, all overloads and anonymous events if present, and record reachable-state restrictions. Fuzz inputs across their declared domains without claiming exhaustive enumeration. Keep a deliberate wrong-topic or wrong-data specimen that the comparison rejects. The bundle contains `test/fizz/`, the emitter inventory, exact commands, tool versions, seed, runs, source SHA and all counterexamples; an unresolved divergence prevents a fidelity claim.

- The mapping from deployed instance types to source contracts, including hooks, role providers and other contracts whose layout or selectors must remain fixed. State how the source revision was matched to the deployed code and identify any gaps.

A maintainer must identify the intended estate. The implementer then derives and records the protected set from its source and deployment evidence. The linked target-registry child owns target identification before Gate 1.
